analysis: Examined the protocol-messages.md head excerpt and the CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift patch plus base text. The change adds a close-code-aware reconnect policy. runLoop now uses a CoordinatorSessionRecorder and policy.nextDelayRange(after:). Code 1012 uses a randomized serviceRestartDelayRange with no backoff growth. A session that stayed open for stableSessionDuration resets the backoff. The receive loop now extracts NWProtocolWebSocket.Metadata inside the receiveMessage callback and records the close code, read from the 2-byte big-endian payload when Network.framework reports noStatusReceived. The close payload is no longer treated as JSON; the .close opcode still throws connectionClosed before handleIncomingFrame, so no new parsing path for untrusted data opens up. The close reason is not read. Security-relevant observations: (1) The close code comes from the coordinator, which is trusted in this model, and it only affects reconnect timing (availability, not authorization, encryption or attestation). A network-path attacker without TLS could inject a close frame, but that is bounded by jitter and the existing reconnect behavior. A 1012 sequence could keep the reconnect delay short and so cause reconnect load on the coordinator. The impact is bounded by serviceRestartDelayRange and the stable-session reset, whose values are in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift (not supplied). I could not verify the lower bound of that range, so there is no finding. (2) Every reconnect still sends a fresh register, and the sessionRegistered, drain-barrier and capacity-session resets in the defer block are unchanged, so T-053 style stale-authorization handling is unaffected. (3) The logged close_code is a numeric value only and leaks nothing. (4) The patch excerpt is incomplete and the new CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorSessionRecorder source was not supplied, so the actual delay ranges, thread-safety of the recorder (written on connectionQueue, read in runLoop) and the reset semantics remain unverified. The documentation hunk matches the code description. No threat model asset, boundary or mitigation appears regressed.
